observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with light-blue walls, a long mirrored wall fitted with a wooden ballet barre, several framed pictures mounted high on the wall, and a pale gray floor marked with dark lines. A woman with dark hair pulled into a bun, wearing a black spaghetti-strap top and a long pink wrap skirt with a green sash and green underlayer, is barefoot and facing the mirror; her full reflection appears in the mirror to the right. The camera viewpoint is fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The dancer performs a continuous sequence of slow, controlled movements in place: she alternates arm positions (extending one arm outward, bending the other, raising both arms overhead, then lowering them), lifts and sets down her feet, and rotates her torso and head.
Her pink skirt and green sash sway and fold in response to her body turns and foot lifts, draping differently from frame to frame.
Her reflection in the mirror tracks her movements as a mirrored image (not a second person), showing the same gestures from the front.
Her feet remain mostly planted in the same area of the floor; the visible motion is body articulation and arm gestures rather than travel across the room.
The background (mirrors, barre, framed pictures, floor lines) stays in fixed screen positions, indicating no camera movement.

At the start her left arm is extended sideways and her right arm bent; mid-sequence she stands with arms low at her sides; later she extends both arms outward and upward in an open pose; near the end she raises her hands toward her head and then lowers them while lifting one foot behind her.
outside_clip_unknowns: The beginning and end of the choreography (the excerpt is cut at both ends, so the dance is already in progress at frame 1 and continues past frame 41).
Any audio, music, or instructional context accompanying the movement.
The dancer's intent (practice vs. performance) and the name/style of the dance.
uncertain_details: Exact tempo and naming of the steps are not determinable from stills alone.
Whether the slight shift in her position relative to the floor lines is a small step or a body rotation is hard to confirm frame by frame.
